items.name: web.search
items.kind: Host API method · iframe surface (+ executa reverse-RPC twin `web/search`)
items.direction: Bundle (iframe) → Host RPC → app_web_facade.web_search → web_service → provider chain (tavily → ddgs)
items.summary: Search the web (or news) **on the user's behalf** — your bundle never holds a search-provider API key. The host owns provider routing, quota, billing and audit; the response schema is provider-agnostic. `search_depth: "advanced"` expresses a *quality intent* (paid tier, ≈28 CU) — the host may degrade to basic (≈0.5–14 CU) and reports the actually-executed tier in `provider_tier`, billing the cheaper rate. Requires manifest `ui.host_api.web` to include `search` (or `*`) AND the user-enabled per-app `web_grant` — the first call returns `APP_NOT_GRANTED`, which your app should treat as the trigger for the host consent card, then retry.

max_results.description: Capped by min(20, web_grant.maxResultsPerCall). Values above the cap are REJECTED (APP_INVALID_REQUEST), never silently truncated.

search_depth.description: advanced requires web_grant.allowAdvanced (explicit user opt-in — real upstream cost).

items.result_shape: { results: [{title, url, snippet, site, published_at?, score?}], provider_tier: "basic"|"advanced", quota_consumed: number }

errors.when: manifest missing ui.host_api.web `search`, or web_grant disabled / allowSearch=false / advanced without allowAdvanced
the whole provider chain failed (call is NOT billed)

items.billing: Main CU pool, per-call: quota = max(provider_cost_usd × QUOTA_COST_RATIO, floor_cu). ddgs basic = 0.5 CU floor; tavily basic ≈ 13.8 CU; tavily advanced ≈ 27.6 CU (at 80% margin — admin margin changes propagate automatically). Billed by the ACTUALLY-executed provider: an advanced request degraded to ddgs bills 0.5 CU. Ledger: LLMRequestType.APP_WEB_SEARCH, model_name="web:{provider}:{op}".
items.notes: `score`/`published_at` are optional — never assume they exist. Results are provider-agnostic; you cannot select a provider. SDK default timeout for the `web` namespace is 60s (override per-call via `{ timeoutMs }`).

items.name: web.fetch
items.kind: Host API method · iframe surface (+ executa reverse-RPC twin `web/fetch`)
items.direction: Bundle (iframe) → Host RPC → app_web_facade.web_fetch → web_service → native SSRF-guarded fetcher (httpx + trafilatura)
items.summary: Fetch 1–10 URLs and get back extracted main content (Markdown or plain text, navigation/ads stripped) with **per-item failure isolation** — one blocked or broken page never fails the batch; check `pages[i].ok`. The host fetcher enforces a hard SSRF policy that CANNOT be disabled: http/https only, port allow-list (80/443/8080/8443), DNS-resolve-then-check against private/reserved/metadata ranges, and full re-validation on every redirect hop (≤5).

max_chars.description: Per-page truncation. Executa (stdio) twin is capped at 8,000/page.

items.result_shape: { pages: [{url, final_url?, ok, title?, content?, published_at?, truncated?, error?}], quota_consumed: number } — pages[] is same length & order as input urls[]. error values: SSRF_BLOCKED | TIMEOUT | HTTP_<status> | PARSE_FAILED | TOO_LARGE | UNSUPPORTED_CONTENT_TYPE:<ct> | TOO_MANY_REDIRECTS | RESPONSE_BUDGET_EXCEEDED

errors.when: manifest missing ui.host_api.web `fetch`, or web_grant disabled / allowFetch=false

items.billing: 1.0 CU floor per URL (native fetcher; ≈zero upstream cost — the floor covers bandwidth/abuse surface). With web_grant.allowAdvanced, failed pages are retried through tavily extract (≈2.76 CU/URL at 80% margin) and billed per actually-used provider. Ledger: LLMRequestType.APP_WEB_FETCH.
items.notes: Whole-response budget is 512 KB (iframe) / 256 KB (executa stdio); overflow pages are kept in-order and marked RESPONSE_BUDGET_EXCEEDED. Only text/html, text/plain and application/xhtml+xml are parsed. No JS rendering, no login-wall bypass — best-effort robots respect. Recommend passing `{ timeoutMs: 90000 }` for large batches.

items.name: web.image_search
items.kind: Host API method · iframe surface (+ executa reverse-RPC twin `web/image_search`)
items.direction: Bundle (iframe) → Host RPC → app_web_facade.web_image_search → web_service → provider chain (serper Google Images → ddgs.images → tavily include_images)
items.summary: Search the web for images through the host's managed providers. **Safe-search is force-enabled platform-side and cannot be disabled** (passing `safe_search: false` is rejected). Results are provider-agnostic; `width`/`height`/`thumbnail_url`/`license_hint` are optional — never assume they exist. `license_hint` is a best-effort passthrough: the platform makes NO copyright warranty; usage-rights judgement stays with your app. Requires manifest `ui.host_api.web` to include `image_search` (or `*`) AND the user's `web_grant.allowImageSearch` — which defaults OFF even when web is enabled (drive the consent card on `APP_NOT_GRANTED`). SDK also accepts the camelCase alias `anna.web.imageSearch`.

max_results.description: Capped by min(50, web_grant.maxResultsPerCall). Values above the cap are REJECTED (APP_INVALID_REQUEST).

min_width.description: Best-effort: results without known dimensions are dropped when a hard constraint is set.

items.result_shape: { results: [{image_url, thumbnail_url?, source_url, title?, width?, height?, mime_type?, license_hint?}], quota_consumed: number, cached?: boolean }

errors.when: manifest missing ui.host_api.web `image_search`, or web_grant disabled / allowImageSearch=false (defaults OFF)
the whole provider chain failed (call is NOT billed)

items.billing: Main CU pool, per-call: serper (Google Images; preferred when key configured) ≈ 3.4 CU at 80% margin; ddgs images = 0.5 CU floor; tavily include_images ≈ 13.8 CU at 80% margin. Billed by the ACTUALLY-executed provider. Results are cached 10 min (sha256 of query+params); cache hits bill the floor CU only and set `cached: true`. Ledger: LLMRequestType.APP_WEB_IMAGE_SEARCH, model_name="web:{provider}:image_search".
items.notes: Rendering result thumbnails requires your bundle CSP to allow the source origins (e.g. csp_overrides img-src https:). The host does not proxy thumbnail bytes — use web.image_fetch to obtain a stored copy.

items.name: web.image_fetch
items.kind: Host API method · iframe surface (+ executa reverse-RPC twin `web/image_fetch`)
items.direction: Bundle (iframe) → Host RPC → app_web_facade.web_image_fetch → web_service → native SSRF-guarded downloader → APS files (app self-scope)
items.summary: Download one image **host-side** into the app's APS file storage and get back an artifact REFERENCE — `path` plus a short-lived `get_url` (30 min) — never bytes. The download enforces the same non-negotiable SSRF policy as web.fetch (scheme/port allow-list, DNS-resolve-then-check, per-redirect-hop re-validation) plus an image MIME whitelist (jpeg/png/webp/gif) verified by MAGIC BYTES, not the Content-Type header. The stored object counts against the user's APS storage quota and follows normal files.* lifecycle (re-presign via anna.files.download_url, delete via anna.files.delete). Requires manifest `ui.host_api.web` `image_fetch` AND `web_grant.allowImageFetch` (defaults OFF). SDK alias: `anna.web.imageFetch`.

purpose.description: Optional audit label (recorded in the usage ledger + artifact metadata).

items.result_shape: { path: string, get_url: string, mime_type: string, bytes_size: number, sha256: string, source_url: string, final_url: string, quota_consumed: number } — note the field is get_url (files.* convention), not url

errors.when: manifest missing ui.host_api.web `image_fetch`, or web_grant disabled / allowImageFetch=false (defaults OFF)
CU pool exhausted OR APS storage quota exceeded
bad url / out-of-range max_bytes / SSRF-blocked target (message starts with SSRF_BLOCKED)
download failed (HTTP_4xx/5xx, TIMEOUT, TOO_LARGE, UNSUPPORTED_IMAGE_TYPE, TOO_MANY_REDIRECTS) — NOT billed

items.billing: 1.0 CU floor per image (native downloader; ≈zero upstream cost) + the stored bytes count against the APS storage quota. Failed downloads are never billed. Ledger: LLMRequestType.APP_WEB_IMAGE_FETCH, model_name="web:native:image_fetch".
items.notes: Executa twin (`web/image_fetch`) stores to the tool scope instead of the app scope and is stdio-frame safe by construction (reference only). Rendering `get_url` in an iframe needs img-src to allow the R2 host — the host auto-injects it into your bundle CSP when the manifest declares web `image_fetch`.

items.name: web_grant
items.direction: User consent UI → custom_config.web_grant → checked by app_web_facade / executa_web_gate on every call
items.summary: Per-app (and per-executa) user consent for web access. Default is DISABLED — unlike embed, web calls have real upstream cost and crawling side effects, so the first `web.*` call returns `APP_NOT_GRANTED` to drive the consent-card flow. Shape: `{enabled, allowSearch, allowFetch, allowAdvanced, allowImageSearch, allowImageFetch, maxResultsPerCall}`. `allowSearch`/`allowFetch` default true once `enabled`; `allowAdvanced` defaults false (paid tier); `allowImageSearch`/`allowImageFetch` default false (Phase 2 — real crawl cost / storage side effects). Usage is metered by the CU pool only.
items.notes: App-side editing: Installed-Apps permission modal (PATCH /api/v1/apps/{id}/grants, `web_grant` key — clamped against manifest ui.host_api.web). Executa-side: the executa Permissions modal (requires manifest host_capabilities web.search/web.fetch to be in manifest_cache — re-register after adding them). `anna-app dev` installs seed a fully-enabled dev web_grant (dev calls are never billed).
